objective: Close service-media replacement, superseded-object cleanup and abandoned-draft cleanup lifecycle without reopening browser authority.

rootCause.summary: The browser owns mutable Storage writes and owner-scoped public.service_media DML while service versions preserve only public URL strings, so object replacement, version promotion and cleanup do not share one canonical authority.
rootCause.versionMediaReference: public URL strings embedded in service_versions.snapshot.images
rootCause.catalogProjection: approval deletes and rebuilds public.service_media from snapshot URL strings
rootCause.atomicBoundary: missing across upload reservation, Storage object, service version, catalog projection and cleanup

stagingObservation.interpretation: The current staging sample is internally referenced, but no schema, operation or job guarantees that invariant after replacement or interrupted submission.

risks: Browser can overwrite a deterministic object path before the corresponding service version is accepted, changing bytes behind a URL preserved by historical snapshots.
Browser can update or delete owner Storage objects without a server transaction that also reconciles service_media and service_versions.
Browser-role DML remains available on public.service_media for owner rows, creating a second mutation path beside moderation approval.
A failed submit_service_for_review call after upload leaves an object without a consumed upload intent or deterministic cleanup authority.
A replaced object has no canonical superseded state or retention window.
Cleanup cannot prove that an object is unreferenced by approved, pending or historical service versions before deletion.
requiredClosure: Introduce server-generated signed upload intents behind the JWT-verified self-service Edge authority.
Generate immutable unique object paths and prohibit browser-selected replacement paths and upsert.
Consume an upload intent when submitting a service version and persist canonical object identity instead of trusting arbitrary public URLs.
Remove direct browser INSERT, UPDATE and DELETE authority from public.service_media.
Remove direct browser Storage UPDATE and DELETE authority; retire direct INSERT after signed upload cutover.
Track prepared, consumed, active, superseded and cleanup-eligible media states canonically.
Project approved media into public.service_media only from canonical consumed assets.
Delete objects only through the Storage API after a reference-safe server check across services, service_media and every service_versions snapshot.
Expire abandoned upload intents deterministically and process cleanup through a permanent server worker or controlled operation.
Add deterministic runtime, structural and SQL validation gates and validate only in staging before documentary closure.
